candidates.title: Dave's released COMMITMENT_BUDGET / log2step(0)=38 are sized on an average uarch density of ~566 usteps per mcycle, but an FP guest runs ~3600, so the honest uarch-level claim cannot be built in the budget and every forced inner delegation drains the honest root clock (with no censorship at all on a devnet, the honest claim is eliminated)
candidates.component: Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 released arbitration constants (prt/contracts/src/arbitration-config/ArbitrationConstants.sol COMMITMENT_BUDGET = 120 minutes, log2step = [38, 0], height = [54, 38]; ClockBudgets.maxAllowance/refill; Tournament.joinTournament lateness deduction, MatchClocks.childReturnAllowance refill) together with the uarch-level claim builder collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes whose cost they must cover
candidates.role: Referee model, as the deployed referee (AUDIT.md component table: Dave prt/contracts with released constants). The emulator's per-ustep cost is what the semantics require (not an emulator defect).
candidates.location: bugs/harness/work/dave/released/prt/contracts/src/arbitration-config/ArbitrationConstants.sol (COMMITMENT_BUDGET, log2step, height); .../arbitration-config/ClockBudgets.sol (maxAllowance = C + 2G + (L-1)(T + 2G), refill = T + 2G); .../tournament/libs/Clock.sol initializePausedAt (join lateness deducted from the inner allowance); .../tournament/libs/MatchClocks.sol childReturnAllowance (refill capped at T + 2G); derivation in bugs/harness/work/dave/released/docs/measurements/constants.md ('clocks price the trusted app's AVERAGE density', density label 566 usteps per big cycle, 173 big cycles/s, 60-minute derivation, deployed with 120 minutes for double slack); script/Deployment.s.sol (censorship 1 week mainnet, 8 hours testnet, 0 devnet; inclusion 5 minutes).
candidates.description: With levels=2 and log2step(0)=38, every root match that seals goes to an inner (leaf) tournament whose commitment is the uarch cycle computation hash of one 2^18-mcycle period (2^38 uarch positions). The honest operator must build it (collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes, one state root hash per executed uarch cycle) and join before the inner tournament closes at seal + max(r1, r2); its join lateness is deducted from its inner clock (Clock.initializePausedAt) and the parent refills at most T + 2G when the child returns (childReturnAllowance), where T = COMMITMENT_BUDGET = 120 min. Dave derived T from a workload whose density is 566 usteps per mcycle (constants.md), which is the uarch's floor: a plain addi loop already measures 550 usteps/mcycle here. The guest controls density: a loop of fdiv.d (softfloat in the uarch) runs a deterministic 3600 usteps per mcycle (max 4361), fsqrt.d 3098, a mixed FP loop 3112 (max 4450), i.e. 5.5-6.4x the sized density; the build cost is linear in executed usteps (measured: 8.5 ms/mcycle for the addi loop vs 45.4 ms/mcycle for the FP loop on this host, 5.3x). With Dave's own throughput figure (173 big cycles/s at 566 density, i.e. ~98k hashed usteps/s) a 2^18-mcycle period at 3600 usteps/mcycle takes ~161 minutes without the hardware slack of 2 that the derivation itself applies, ~321 minutes with it, against T = 120 minutes. Each forced delegation therefore costs the correct claim the overrun (41-201 minutes) out of its censorship budget C, which ClockBudgets reserves for censorship alone, and the refill never returns it. With C = 0 (Deployment.s.sol devnet: 'their clocks cover only the honest path (every action within one inclusion, every build within the commitment budget)'), the root allowance is 2G + (T + 2G) = 700 blocks (140 min at 12 s), so the inner tournament of the first delegation closes about 140 minutes after the seal, before the honest uarch claim (>= 161 min) can join; the inner tournament is then won by the adversary's claim ending at the dishonest contested state (or has no honest-side winner), the honest mcycle claim is eliminated and the dishonest root claim wins. On a testnet (C = 8 h) a handful of forced delegations (2-11 depending on slack) exhaust C with no censorship; on mainnet each delegation silently removes 41-201 minutes from the one-week censorship tolerance.
candidates.trigger: Dishonest claimant plus guest code (input sender, or simply an application that does floating-point work): (1) an input makes the guest run an FP-heavy loop (e.g. fdiv.d) through some 2^18-mcycle period, or the application does so legitimately; (2) the claimant posts a root claim that lies at the first leaf after that period (e.g. the honest trajectory with that one leaf changed, as the manual's 'fabulist'); bisection converges there and sealInnerMatchAndCreateInnerTournament opens the inner tournament over the FP-dense period; (3) the claimant joins its own inner claim immediately (it can precompute it) and lets the honest operator build its 2^38-leaf uarch claim. Repeat with further Sybil root claims to force more delegations.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from any valid template: the guest is fully adversarial after reading an input (THREAT_MODEL section 4) and any assignment of guest-writable registers/instruction stream is presumed reachable (section 2); even without subversion, a correctly designed FP-heavy application (numeric Python, etc.) produces this density on honest inputs. The density figures are deterministic uarch cycle counts (run_uarch per mcycle) on a bare-metal M-mode guest with mstatus.FS enabled; the same instructions run identically under Linux in U-mode. The adversary steers the dispute to that period (section 7: 'Steer the dispute to any position of the honest computation, and force the honest claim through a logarithmic number of matches').
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? No exclusion fits. The trigger is a guest instruction stream plus dishonest claims, both adversary capabilities (sections 4 and 7). The deployment-obligation exclusion does not apply: 'Defects that need the deployment to violate one of A1 to A8, unless ... or unless an implementation of the referee model is what violates it (section 3)', and Dave with its released constants is the referee model as the deployed referee (AUDIT.md). It is not 'average-case performance': the defect is a worst-case cost. 2. Role: Dave's released constants and clock rules play the referee-model role, 'rated as if a deployed referee had it. Which claim a timeout or an elimination decides is part of what it derives.' The emulator's cost per ustep is what the semantics require ('A cost that the specified semantics require is not a defect'), so the defect is the sizing, not the emulator. 3. High/Medium cases: possibly the section 3 clause 'A defect that only changes how long a claim may take to respond ... is rated as support', which would cap it at Medium as a support defect (it would be Critical in the role it stands in for). Against that reading: the result is not only a changed window. The deployed referee eliminates the honest claim and a dishonest claim wins, which is 'what it derives'. No unreachable state is involved. 4. Critical: A7 is violated at a reachable state: 'The dispute constants and clocks leave room for the honest claim to play the logarithmic number of matches that a tournament forces on it, at the worst-case costs of R12 ... No rule of the referee may make the honest claim lose by timeout while it acts within its own clock.' R12 lists 'a uarch-level claim' as an operation whose worst case must be covered, and section 8 makes Critical 'An operation listed in R12 whose worst-case cost a guest can make unbounded, super-linear, or larger than what the deployment was sized for'. Dave sizes on 'the trusted app's AVERAGE density', while R4 requires completeness 'for every guest, whether or not its application is correctly designed ... at the costs of R12 for the mcycles the guest actually runs'. Deciding facts: whether triage applies the 'only changes how long a claim may take to respond' clause to the deployed Dave constants (Medium) or treats the referee's elimination of the honest claim as derived (Critical), and whether devnet/testnet parameter sets count as deployments. On mainnet parameters alone it is at least a High-style margin removal: a constant-factor (5-6x) increase in the worst case of an R12 operation beyond the sizing, which consumes the censorship tolerance ('removes a margin that the goal relies on').
candidates.claimed_severity: Critical (A7/R12, deployed referee sizing; honest claim eliminated on the released devnet parameters with no censorship, and on testnet parameters after a few forced delegations). Medium if triage applies the 'only changes how long a claim may take to respond' support clause.
candidates.threat_to_goal: Section 1 goal: the honest operator runs on the resources the deployment was sized for and its transactions are included within the clocks, but it cannot build its uarch-level claim within the clock the referee grants. The inner tournament then closes without the honest uarch claim, the adversary's uarch claim at the dishonest contested state wins, the honest mcycle claim is eliminated and a dishonest root claim settles a state that differs from the one the state transition function defines. This is the completeness failure of section 1: 'cannot respond in time. If the honest claim is eliminated, a dishonest claim can win.' Where C is large (mainnet), the same mechanism silently spends the censorship tolerance that A7 and Dave's own ClockBudgets reserve for censorship.
candidates.evidence: Scratch dir /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERCLAIMANT/: bare-metal guests assembled with llvm-mc (base.S addi loop, fp.S mixed fsqrt/fdiv/fmadd loop, div.S fdiv.d loop, sqrt.S, ...), density.lua (loads the raw binary at 0x80000000 with 64 MiB RAM, runs 100 mcycles, then for 2000 mcycles calls run_uarch(UARCH_CYCLE_MAX), reads uarch_cycle, reset_uarch; optionally times collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes over 2000 mcycles). Results with the in-tree build (bugs/env.sh): base addi avg 550.0 usteps/mcycle; fp mixed avg 3111.9 (max 4450); fdiv.d avg 3600.0 (max 4361); fsqrt.d 3098.4; collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes 8.52 ms/mcycle (addi, 37 min per 2^18 mcycles) vs 45.36 ms/mcycle (fp mixed, 198 min per 2^18 mcycles) on this shared 4-CPU host. Dave's derivation (docs/measurements/constants.md) uses density 566 and 173 big cycles/s with hardware slack 2 for a 60-minute table, deployed at 120 minutes. Arithmetic for the devnet parameters (Deployment.s.sol: 12 s blocks, inclusion 5 min = 25 blocks, C = 0, T = 600 blocks): maxAllowance = 0 + 2*25 + (600 + 50) = 700 blocks = 140 min, while the uarch claim of an fdiv-dense period takes >= 161 min at Dave's measured throughput.
candidates.test_idea: Deterministic, no wall-clock timing: build the fdiv.d bare-metal guest (4 x fdiv.d; j loop, mstatus.FS set), run 2000 mcycles and count uarch cycles per mcycle with run_uarch/reset_uarch (deterministic result 3600). Read COMMITMENT_BUDGET, log2step(0) and the sized density from the released Dave sources (566 usteps per big cycle in docs/measurements/constants.md, or the throughput * budget product it implies: 173/s * 2 slack^-1 ... * 7200 s >= 2^18 big cycles at density 566). Assert that the uarch work Dave budgets for one inner commitment (2^log2step(0) uarch positions, of which density/2^20 are executed, i.e. 2^18 * 566 executed usteps) is at least 2^18 * measured_density (it is 2^18 * 3600), i.e. exit 1 because the guest-controlled worst case exceeds the sizing by 6.4x. A chain-level variant: deploy the released Dave build with devnet parameters on the harness anvil, seal a root match at a period of the fdiv guest, mine blocks at the rate the honest build consumes them (blocks = build_usteps / Dave's 98k usteps/s / 12 s), and assert the honest uarch claim can still join before the inner tournament closes (it cannot: 140 min window).
candidates.notes: Dave documents the choice ('clocks price the trusted app's AVERAGE density; coordinates stay worst-case', docs/measurements/constants.md and docs/dimensioning.md), so triage must decide whether the threat model's A7/R12 worst-case requirement overrides that documented deployment assumption. A deterministic test needs no timing: the gap is a ratio of deterministic uarch cycle counts (3600/566 = 6.4x) against a budget whose own derivation states a 2x hardware slack and a 2x double slack (4x total).

not_covered: Exhaustive search for the maximum uarch cycles per mcycle (page walks with TLB misses, AMOs, interrupts and traps per instruction, misaligned accesses under Linux); I measured only FP loops (max observed 4450 per mcycle).
Gas measurements of honest transactions (winLeafMatch with a 64 KiB input delivery, sealing, joins) against real block gas limits; the EVM harness disables limits.
A chain-level reproduction on the released Dave build (deploy with devnet/testnet clock parameters, force delegations, mine blocks): only arithmetic from the released constants plus emulator timings.

The soundness of the regenerated UArchStep.sol against the C++ uarch for every instruction and for memory-map traps (R3/R10). I checked only the log-consumption and Merkle-authentication framework (AccessLogs, Buffer, Memory, SendCmioResponse, UArchReset, CartesiStateTransition), which looked sound.
The off-chain verify functions (C/Lua/JSON-RPC) with crafted logs, which the referee model in doc/recipes calls.
prtu.lua and game-transport.lua beyond request_first_valid and request_all (malformed or oversized JSON, resource exhaustion of the model referee server).
prt-bridge.lua asserts on adversarial chain events, which could crash the support bridge.
Bond, refund and recovery economics (Bond.sol, Gas.sol, tryRecoveringBond), which the threat model does not cover.
The cartesi-rollups Application output execution paths beyond validateOutputHash, and the sentry and foreclosure flows of DaveConsensus.

Dave's multi-delegation delay bound (docs/prt-delay-bound.md): how many sequential root matches asynchronous pairing can force on the honest claim before root closure, which sets the exact Sybil count the testnet and mainnet variants need.
